Background and Design Motivation\n8\t\n9\tPhase 1 (`task-047`) establishes the architectural contract for chunk-based decomposition before solver kernels are wired to a runtime executor. The goal is to define what a chunk owns, how chunks expose halo and monitor metadata, how chunk placement maps onto devices or nodes, and how this avoids blocking later systolic or overlapped execution phases.\n10\t\n11\t### Reference Foundations\n12\t\n13\t- **Meep chunk architecture** (`../meep/doc/docs/Chunks_and_Symmetry.md`): chunk is the stable decomposition unit, not MPI rank. A rank may own multiple chunks. Chunk boundaries align with PML layers and symmetry planes, not with MPI ranks. Communication plans are stage-specific and component-family-specific.\n14\t- **Systolic FDTD scheduling** (`papers/systolic_fdtd.pdf`): the important architectural seam is the split between chunk-local interior work, lower-dimensional boundary exchange, and a pluggable execution policy. Per-face, per-stage halo semantics and interior-versus-boundary planning must be explicit now so future systolic or overlapped execution can be added without redesign.\n15\t- **Phase 1 codebase state**: `CompiledSimulation` in `compiler/pipeline.py` treats the entire grid as one monolithic entity. `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` is a global constant. No chunk index, rank, ownership mask, or per-chunk field decomposition exists yet.\n16\t\n17\t### Design Principles\n18\t\n19\t1. **Chunk is the unit of parallelism.** Rank or device is placement, not computation.\n20\t2. **Logical and stored topology diverge.** Symmetry reduction and periodic/Bloch remapping are logical-address transforms over a full-domain view, not data-layout changes.\n21\t3. **Scene compilation is separate from stepping.** Geometry and material initialization produce coefficient fields; those fields are then chunked for execution.\n22\t4. **Bulk-synchronous by default, systolic-ready by design.** Phase 1 is bulk-synchronous, but chunk metadata and runtime orchestration preserve per-face, per-stage halo semantics so overlap can be layered in later without rearchitecting the chunk contract.\n23\t5. **Halo depth is per-face, not global.** Different boundary families (PML, ABC, Bloch, periodic) require different halo widths and different exchange semantics.\n24\t\n25\t---\n26\t\n27\t## 2. Chunk Data Model\n28\t\n29\t### 2.1 ChunkSpec — Planning Metadata\n30\t\n31\t`ChunkSpec` is a frozen planning metadata object produced during scene compilation (not a runtime data structure). It describes the intended decomposition before any field buffers are allocated.\n32\t\n33\t```python\n34\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n35\tclass ChunkSpec:\n36\t    \"\"\"Planning metadata for one chunk — produced during compilation.\"\"\"\n37\t\n38\t    chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int]          # logical position in chunk grid\n39\t    global_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]            # full-domain bounds of this chunk (lo, hi)\n40\t    interior_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]          # interior (non-halo) cell index range\n41\t    owned_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]              # cells this chunk updates (including boundary)\n42\t    local_grid_shape: tuple[int, int, int]       # full local array shape incl. ghost cells\n43\t\n44\t    # Per-face halo metadata\n45\t    face_halos: dict[str, FaceHalo]              # key: \"x.minus\", \"x.plus\", \"y.minus\", ...\n46\t\n47\t    # Symmetry metadata\n48\t    is_reduced: bool                             # True if chunk is in symmetry-reduced region\n49\t    symmetry_multiplicity: int                   # how many full-domain points this chunk represents\n50\t\n51\t    # Ownership flags for sources and monitors\n52\t    source_indices: tuple[int, ...]             # indices into compiled_sources owned here\n53\t    monitor_indices: tuple[int, ...]              # indices into compiled_monitors owned here\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\t**Key invariants:**\n57\t- `interior_bounds` defines the region this chunk updates without reading halo data.\n58\t- `owned_bounds` includes the one-cell-wide boundary ring that this chunk writes and other chunks read.\n59\t- `local_grid_shape` is the shape of the full local array including ghost cells — this is what field buffers are allocated to.\n60\t- For a chunk at chunk_index `(i, j, k)`, the global cell index range of its interior is `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` in grid coordinates.\n61\t\n62\t### 2.2 FaceHalo — Per-Face Halo Descriptor\n63\t\n64\t```python\n65\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n66\tclass FaceHalo:\n67\t    \"\"\"Halo metadata for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n68\t\n69\t    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n70\t    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n71\t    depth: int                                  # number of ghost cells on this face\n72\t    neighbor_chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int] | None  # None = domain boundary\n73\t    exchange_kind: Literal[\n74\t        \"periodic\", \"bloch\", \"pec\", \"pmc\",\n75\t        \"pml\", \"stable_pml\", \"absorber\", \"abc\",\n76\t        \"symmetry_copy\", \"interior\"\n77\t    ]\n78\t    phase_factor: complex = 1.0 + 0.0j          # for Bloch: e^{i k · d}\n79\t    electric_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n80\t    magnetic_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n81\t    pml_profile: PMLFaceProfile | None = None   # for PML faces: coefficient profiles\n82\t    abc_coefficients: ABCFaceCoefficients | None = None  # for ABC faces\n83\t```\n84\t\n85\t**Exchange kinds:**\n86\t- `periodic`: copy from neighbor's `plus` face to my `minus` ghost (or vice versa)\n87\t- `bloch`: same as periodic but multiply by `phase_factor` (complex conjugate on minus side for H, no conjugate on E per Maxwell's convention)\n88\t- `pec`: set ghost E to `-E_interior` reflected; H ghost from `+H_interior`\n89\t- `pmc`: opposite parity of PEC\n90\t- `pml` / `stable_pml` / `absorber`: staged damping update applied in PML stage (see Section 5)\n91\t- `abc`: first-order Engquist-Majda absorption via one-step recurrence\n92\t- `symmetry_copy`: fill ghost from interior using electric/magnetic sign transforms\n93\t- `interior`: no exchange — this face is adjacent to another local chunk (same process/device)\n94\t\n95\t### 2.3 ChunkLayout — Global Decomposition Plan\n96\t\n97\t```python\n98\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n99\tclass ChunkLayout:\n100\t    \"\"\"Global chunk decomposition plan — immutable after compilation.\"\"\"\n101\t\n102\t    num_chunks: tuple[int, int, int]           # chunks per axis\n103\t    total_chunks: int                          # product of above\n104\t    chunks: tuple[ChunkSpec, ...]               # one per chunk\n105\t    periodic_axes: tuple[str, ...]             # For device/rank mapping\n110\t    device_assignment: tuple[int, ...]         # chunk_index → device_id (for CUDA)\n111\t    rank_assignment: tuple[int, ...]            # chunk_index → MPI rank\n112\t```\n113\t\n114\t**Key property:** `ChunkLayout.total_chunks` is the number of *logical* chunks, not necessarily the number of MPI ranks or CUDA devices. One rank/device may own multiple chunks.\n115\t\n116\t---\n117\t\n118\t## 3. What a Chunk Owns\n119\t\n120\tA chunk is the unit of **field storage and field update**. Each chunk owns:\n121\t\n122\t### 3.1 Field Arrays\n123\t\n124\tFor a chunk with `local_grid_shape = (Nx, Ny, Nz)`:\n125\t\n126\t| Array | Shape | Staggering |\n127\t|---|---|---|\n128\t| `electric_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee electric cell centers |\n129\t| `magnetic_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee magnetic cell centers |\n130\t| `eps_xx`, `eps_yy`, `eps_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permittivity on E-grid |\n131\t| `mu_xx`, `mu_yy`, `mu_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permeability on H-grid |\n132\t| `sigma_e` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | electric conductivity |\n133\t| `sigma_h` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | magnetic conductivity |\n134\t\n135\t**Note:** These are *local* arrays including ghost cells. The interior region `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` contains valid owned field values. Ghost cells are filled by the boundary exchange stage before each update.\n136\t\n137\t### 3.2 Dispersive Auxiliary state\n138\t\n139\tFor PoleResidue media, per pole per component:\n140\t\n141\t```\n142\tpol_x[p, i, j, k], pol_y[p, i, j, k], pol_z[p, i, j, k]  # polarization currents\n143\t```\n144\t\n145\tShape: `(num_poles, Nx, Ny, Nz)` per component axis. These are allocated only for chunks that contain dispersive material.\n146\t\n147\t### 3.3 Anisotropic Auxiliary State\n148\t\n149\tFor diagonal AnisotropicMedia, the six `eps_xx` etc. arrays above are sufficient (no extra auxiliary state). If Phase 2 introduces fully anisotropic media, additional off-diagonal arrays would be needed.\n150\t\n151\t### 3.4 PML/ABC Boundary state\n152\t\n153\tPer face with PML/ABC:\n154\t\n155\t```\n156\tPML memory: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]   # shape from PMLFaceState.memory_shape\n157\tABC previous: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]  # shape from ABCFaceState.value_shape\n158\t```\n159\t\n160\tThese are allocated per chunk per absorbing face, not global.\n161\t\n162\t### 3.5 Source State\n163\t\n164\tSources are not stored per chunk persistently. Instead, each chunk's `ChunkSpec.source_indices` tells which sources from `CompiledSources` inject into this chunk's domain. At runtime, source injection kernels use the compiled source metadata (placements, amplitude weights) to add source contributions directly into the chunk's `electric_field` or `magnetic_field` arrays.\n165\t\n166\t### 3.6 Monitor State\n167\t\n168\tSimilarly, monitor recording state is per-chunk. For field monitors:\n169\t- `FieldMonitorState` per monitor that overlaps this chunk\n170\t- DFT accumulation buffers for frequency-domain monitors\n171\t\n172\tFor flux monitors:\n173\t- `FluxMonitorState` per monitor with surfaces intersecting this chunk\n174\t\n175\tChunk-local monitor data is gathered by a monitor collection stage after each recording interval.\n176\t\n177\t---\n178\t\n179\t## 4. Halo and Monitor Metadata\n180\t\n181\t### 4.1 Halo Exchange Protocol\n182\t\n183\tHalo exchange is **stage-specific** and **component-family-specific**, following the pattern established in the boundary compiler but scoped per chunk pair:\n184\t\n185\t```\n186\tTimestep stage order per chunk:\n187\t  1. [boundary_exchange]    — fill ghost cells from neighbors\n188\t  2. [electric_update]       — update E in interior + owned-boundary cells\n189\t  3. [source_injection]      — add source contributions to E\n190\t  4. [boundary_exchange]     — re-exchange E ghosts (needed for H update)\n191\t  5. [magnetic_update]        — update H in interior + owned-boundary cells\n192\t  6. [monitor_collection]     — record E/H at monitor points (interval filter)\n193\t  7. [pml_stage]             — apply PML/ABC damping to E and H ghosts\n194\t  8. [convergence_check]     — (on interval) compute integrated E², check shutoff\n195\t```\n196\t\n197\t**Key property:** The `boundary_exchange` stage operates on ghost cells only. Interior cells are never communicated during the timestep — only at the start of the step for halo fill and after the step for PML memory update.\n198\t\n199\t### 4.2 Halo Depth\n200\t\n201\tHalo depth is **per-face**, not a global constant. Typical depths:\n202\t\n203\t| Boundary Type | Halo Depth | Notes |\n204\t|---|---|---|\n205\t| Periodic / Bloch | 1 cell | standard Yee ghost cell |\n206\t| PEC / PMC | 1 cell | ghost set by reflection transform |\n207\t| PML | variable (num_layers) | full PML depth, staggered |\n208\t| ABC (first-order) | 1 cell | single-step recurrence |\n209\t| Symmetry | 1 cell | copy from interior with sign transform |\n210\t| Interior (chunk neighbor) | 1 cell | local memory copy |\n211\t\n212\t**The current `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` must be replaced** with per-face `FaceHalo.depth` from the `ChunkLayout`.\n213\t\n214\t### 4.3 Monitor Overlap with Chunks\n215\t\n216\tA monitor may span multiple chunks. Monitor metadata in `ChunkSpec.monitor_indices` tells which monitors overlap this chunk. Monitor data is accumulated per-chunk and gathered by a global collection pass.\n217\t\n218\tFor a `FieldMonitor` with interval/start semantics:\n219\t- Each chunk computes which of its interior cells fall within the monitor's spatial region\n220\t- Recording is done by the chunk that owns the cell\n221\t- Gathered data is assembled in rank-order for `SimulationData`\n222\t\n223\tFor a `FluxMonitor`:\n224\t- The flux surface may be split across multiple chunks\n225\t- Each chunk computes its portion of the Poynting flux integral\n226\t- Partial sums are reduced across chunks\n227\t\n228\t---\n229\t\n230\t## 5. PML / ABC State Decomposition\n231\t\n232\tPML and ABC state must be decomposed per-chunk per-face. The current monolithic `PMLBoundaryState` in the codebase must be replaced.\n233\t\n234\t### 5.1 PML Face State (per chunk, per face)\n235\t\n236\t```python\n237\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n238\tclass ChunkPMLFaceState:\n239\t    \"\"\"PML state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n240\t\n241\t    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n242\t    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n243\t    memory_shape: tuple[int, ...]         # transverse shape of the PML layer\n244\t    sigma_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled sigma (sigma_min..sigma_max polynomial)\n245\t    kappa_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled kappa\n246\t    alpha_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled alpha\n247\t    memory: np.ndarray                      # persistent PML memory (attenuation term)\n248\t```\n249\t\n250\t### 5.2 ABC Face State (per chunk, per face)\n251\t\n252\t```python\n253\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n254\tclass ChunkABCFaceState:\n255\t    \"\"\"First-order ABC state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n256\t\n257\t    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n258\t    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n259\t    value_shape: tuple[int, ...]            # transverse shape of the ABC surface\n260\t    previous_boundary: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep on boundary\n261\t    previous_adjacent: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep one cell inside\n262\t```\n263\t\n264\t---\n265\t\n266\t## 6. Device and Node Placement\n267\t\n268\t### 6.1 CUDA GPU Placement\n269\t\n270\tThe `ChunkLayout.device_assignment` field maps each logical `chunk_index` to a CUDA device ID. For Phase 1 single-GPU or dual-GPU smoke tests:\n271\t\n272\t- All chunks map to device 0 (single-GPU fallback)\n273\t- Or chunks 0..N//2 on device 0, chunks N//2..N on device 1\n274\t\n275\t**This mapping is a planning artifact, not the execution runtime.** The actual field arrays are allocated on the target device via CUDA managed memory or explicit device arrays.\n276\t\n277\t### 6.2 Multi-Node / MPI Placement\n278\t\n279\t`ChunkLayout.rank_assignment` maps each logical chunk to an MPI rank. Phase 1 Chunk Contract and Multi-Node Decomposition Architecture\n\n## Status\n\n**Draft — for review and task handoff**\n\n## 1. Background and Design Motivation\n\nPhase 1 (`task-047`) establishes the architectural contract for chunk-based decomposition before solver kernels are wired to a runtime executor. The goal is to define what a chunk owns, how chunks expose halo and monitor metadata, how chunk placement maps onto devices or nodes, and how this avoids blocking later systolic or overlapped execution phases.\n\n### Reference Foundations\n\n- **Meep chunk architecture** (`../meep/doc/docs/Chunks_and_Symmetry.md`): chunk is the stable decomposition unit, not MPI rank. A rank may own multiple chunks. Chunk boundaries align with PML layers and symmetry planes, not with MPI ranks. Communication plans are stage-specific and component-family-specific.\n- **Systolic FDTD scheduling** (`papers/systolic_fdtd.pdf`): the important architectural seam is the split between chunk-local interior work, lower-dimensional boundary exchange, and a pluggable execution policy. Per-face, per-stage halo semantics and interior-versus-boundary planning must be explicit now so future systolic or overlapped execution can be added without redesign.\n- **Phase 1 codebase state**: `CompiledSimulation` in `compiler/pipeline.py` treats the entire grid as one monolithic entity. `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` is a global constant. No chunk index, rank, ownership mask, or per-chunk field decomposition exists yet.\n\n### Design Principles\n\n1. **Chunk is the unit of parallelism.** Rank or device is placement, not computation.\n2. **Logical and stored topology diverge.** Symmetry reduction and periodic/Bloch remapping are logical-address transforms over a full-domain view, not data-layout changes.\n3. **Scene compilation is separate from stepping.** Geometry and material initialization produce coefficient fields; those fields are then chunked for execution.\n4. **Bulk-synchronous by default, systolic-ready by design.** Phase 1 is bulk-synchronous, but chunk metadata and runtime orchestration preserve per-face, per-stage halo semantics so overlap can be layered in later without rearchitecting the chunk contract.\n5. **Halo depth is per-face, not global.** Different boundary families (PML, ABC, Bloch, periodic) require different halo widths and different exchange semantics.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Chunk Data Model\n\n### 2.1 ChunkSpec — Planning Metadata\n\n`ChunkSpec` is a frozen planning metadata object produced during scene compilation (not a runtime data structure). It describes the intended decomposition before any field buffers are allocated.\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkSpec:\n    \"\"\"Planning metadata for one chunk — produced during compilation.\"\"\"\n\n    chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int]          # logical position in chunk grid\n    global_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]            # full-domain bounds of this chunk (lo, hi)\n    interior_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]          # interior (non-halo) cell index range\n    owned_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]              # cells this chunk updates (including boundary)\n    local_grid_shape: tuple[int, int, int]       # full local array shape incl. ghost cells\n\n    # Per-face halo metadata\n    face_halos: dict[str, FaceHalo]              # key: \"x.minus\", \"x.plus\", \"y.minus\", ...\n\n    # Symmetry metadata\n    is_reduced: bool                             # True if chunk is in symmetry-reduced region\n    symmetry_multiplicity: int                   # how many full-domain points this chunk represents\n\n    # Ownership flags for sources and monitors\n    source_indices: tuple[int, ...]             # indices into compiled_sources owned here\n    monitor_indices: tuple[int, ...]              # indices into compiled_monitors owned here\n```\n\n**Key invariants:**\n- `interior_bounds` defines the region this chunk updates without reading halo data.\n- `owned_bounds` includes the one-cell-wide boundary ring that this chunk writes and other chunks read.\n- `local_grid_shape` is the shape of the full local array including ghost cells — this is what field buffers are allocated to.\n- For a chunk at chunk_index `(i, j, k)`, the global cell index range of its interior is `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` in grid coordinates.\n\n### 2.2 FaceHalo — Per-Face Halo Descriptor\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass FaceHalo:\n    \"\"\"Halo metadata for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n\n    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n    depth: int                                  # number of ghost cells on this face\n    neighbor_chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int] | None  # None = domain boundary\n    exchange_kind: Literal[\n        \"periodic\", \"bloch\", \"pec\", \"pmc\",\n        \"pml\", \"stable_pml\", \"absorber\", \"abc\",\n        \"symmetry_copy\", \"interior\"\n    ]\n    phase_factor: complex = 1.0 + 0.0j          # for Bloch: e^{i k · d}\n    electric_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n    magnetic_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n    pml_profile: PMLFaceProfile | None = None   # for PML faces: coefficient profiles\n    abc_coefficients: ABCFaceCoefficients | None = None  # for ABC faces\n```\n\n**Exchange kinds:**\n- `periodic`: copy from neighbor's `plus` face to my `minus` ghost (or vice versa)\n- `bloch`: same as periodic but multiply by `phase_factor` (complex conjugate on minus side for H, no conjugate on E per Maxwell's convention)\n- `pec`: set ghost E to `-E_interior` reflected; H ghost from `+H_interior`\n- `pmc`: opposite parity of PEC\n- `pml` / `stable_pml` / `absorber`: staged damping update applied in PML stage (see Section 5)\n- `abc`: first-order Engquist-Majda absorption via one-step recurrence\n- `symmetry_copy`: fill ghost from interior using electric/magnetic sign transforms\n- `interior`: no exchange — this face is adjacent to another local chunk (same process/device)\n\n### 2.3 ChunkLayout — Global Decomposition Plan\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkLayout:\n    \"\"\"Global chunk decomposition plan — immutable after compilation.\"\"\"\n\n    num_chunks: tuple[int, int, int]           # chunks per axis\n    total_chunks: int                          # product of above\n    chunks: tuple[ChunkSpec, ...]               # one per chunk\n    periodic_axes: tuple[str, ...]             # axes with periodic/Bloch boundary\n    bloch_axes: tuple[str, ...]                 # axes with Bloch boundary\n    exchange_plan: dict[str, ExchangeDescriptor]  # keyed by (\"chunk_a\", \"chunk_b\", \"face\")\n\n    # For device/rank mapping\n    device_assignment: tuple[int, ...]         # chunk_index → device_id (for CUDA)\n    rank_assignment: tuple[int, ...]            # chunk_index → MPI rank\n```\n\n**Key property:** `ChunkLayout.total_chunks` is the number of *logical* chunks, not necessarily the number of MPI ranks or CUDA devices. One rank/device may own multiple chunks.\n\n---\n\n## 3. What a Chunk Owns\n\nA chunk is the unit of **field storage and field update**. Each chunk owns:\n\n### 3.1 Field Arrays\n\nFor a chunk with `local_grid_shape = (Nx, Ny, Nz)`:\n\n| Array | Shape | Staggering |\n|---|---|---|\n| `electric_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee electric cell centers |\n| `magnetic_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee magnetic cell centers |\n| `eps_xx`, `eps_yy`, `eps_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permittivity on E-grid |\n| `mu_xx`, `mu_yy`, `mu_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permeability on H-grid |\n| `sigma_e` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | electric conductivity |\n| `sigma_h` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | magnetic conductivity |\n\n**Note:** These are *local* arrays including ghost cells. The interior region `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` contains valid owned field values. Ghost cells are filled by the boundary exchange stage before each update.\n\n### 3.2 Dispersive Auxiliary state\n\nFor PoleResidue media, per pole per component:\n\n```\npol_x[p, i, j, k], pol_y[p, i, j, k], pol_z[p, i, j, k]  # polarization currents\n```\n\nShape: `(num_poles, Nx, Ny, Nz)` per component axis. These are allocated only for chunks that contain dispersive material.\n\n### 3.3 Anisotropic Auxiliary State\n\nFor diagonal AnisotropicMedia, the six `eps_xx` etc. arrays above are sufficient (no extra auxiliary state). If Phase 2 introduces fully anisotropic media, additional off-diagonal arrays would be needed.\n\n### 3.4 PML/ABC Boundary state\n\nPer face with PML/ABC:\n\n```\nPML memory: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]   # shape from PMLFaceState.memory_shape\nABC previous: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]  # shape from ABCFaceState.value_shape\n```\n\nThese are allocated per chunk per absorbing face, not global.\n\n### 3.5 Source State\n\nSources are not stored per chunk persistently. Instead, each chunk's `ChunkSpec.source_indices` tells which sources from `CompiledSources` inject into this chunk's domain. At runtime, source injection kernels use the compiled source metadata (placements, amplitude weights) to add source contributions directly into the chunk's `electric_field` or `magnetic_field` arrays.\n\n### 3.6 Monitor State\n\nSimilarly, monitor recording state is per-chunk. For field monitors:\n- `FieldMonitorState` per monitor that overlaps this chunk\n- DFT accumulation buffers for frequency-domain monitors\n\nFor flux monitors:\n- `FluxMonitorState` per monitor with surfaces intersecting this chunk\n\nChunk-local monitor data is gathered by a monitor collection stage after each recording interval.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Halo and Monitor Metadata\n\n### 4.1 Halo Exchange Protocol\n\nHalo exchange is **stage-specific** and **component-family-specific**, following the pattern established in the boundary compiler but scoped per chunk pair:\n\n```\nTimestep stage order per chunk:\n  1. [boundary_exchange]    — fill ghost cells from neighbors\n  2. [electric_update]       — update E in interior + owned-boundary cells\n  3. [source_injection]      — add source contributions to E\n  4. [boundary_exchange]     — re-exchange E ghosts (needed for H update)\n  5. [magnetic_update]        — update H in interior + owned-boundary cells\n  6. [monitor_collection]     — record E/H at monitor points (interval filter)\n  7. [pml_stage]             — apply PML/ABC damping to E and H ghosts\n  8. [convergence_check]     — (on interval) compute integrated E², check shutoff\n```\n\n**Key property:** The `boundary_exchange` stage operates on ghost cells only. Interior cells are never communicated during the timestep — only at the start of the step for halo fill and after the step for PML memory update.\n\n### 4.2 Halo Depth\n\nHalo depth is **per-face**, not a global constant. Typical depths:\n\n| Boundary Type | Halo Depth | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Periodic / Bloch | 1 cell | standard Yee ghost cell |\n| PEC / PMC | 1 cell | ghost set by reflection transform |\n| PML | variable (num_layers) | full PML depth, staggered |\n| ABC (first-order) | 1 cell | single-step recurrence |\n| Symmetry | 1 cell | copy from interior with sign transform |\n| Interior (chunk neighbor) | 1 cell | local memory copy |\n\n**The current `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` must be replaced** with per-face `FaceHalo.depth` from the `ChunkLayout`.\n\n### 4.3 Monitor Overlap with Chunks\n\nA monitor may span multiple chunks. Monitor metadata in `ChunkSpec.monitor_indices` tells which monitors overlap this chunk. Monitor data is accumulated per-chunk and gathered by a global collection pass.\n\nFor a `FieldMonitor` with interval/start semantics:\n- Each chunk computes which of its interior cells fall within the monitor's spatial region\n- Recording is done by the chunk that owns the cell\n- Gathered data is assembled in rank-order for `SimulationData`\n\nFor a `FluxMonitor`:\n- The flux surface may be split across multiple chunks\n- Each chunk computes its portion of the Poynting flux integral\n- Partial sums are reduced across chunks\n\n---\n\n## 5. PML / ABC State Decomposition\n\nPML and ABC state must be decomposed per-chunk per-face. The current monolithic `PMLBoundaryState` in the codebase must be replaced.\n\n### 5.1 PML Face State (per chunk, per face)\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkPMLFaceState:\n    \"\"\"PML state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n\n    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n    memory_shape: tuple[int, ...]         # transverse shape of the PML layer\n    sigma_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled sigma (sigma_min..sigma_max polynomial)\n    kappa_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled kappa\n    alpha_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled alpha\n    memory: np.ndarray                      # persistent PML memory (attenuation term)\n```\n\n### 5.2 ABC Face State (per chunk, per face)\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkABCFaceState:\n    \"\"\"First-order ABC state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n\n    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n    value_shape: tuple[int, ...]            # transverse shape of the ABC surface\n    previous_boundary: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep on boundary\n    previous_adjacent: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep one cell inside\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Device and Node Placement\n\n### 6.1 CUDA GPU Placement\n\nThe `ChunkLayout.device_assignment` field maps each logical `chunk_index` to a CUDA device ID. For Phase 1 single-GPU or dual-GPU smoke tests:\n\n- All chunks map to device 0 (single-GPU fallback)\n- Or chunks 0..N//2 on device 0, chunks N//2..N on device 1\n\n**This mapping is a planning artifact, not the execution runtime.** The actual field arrays are allocated on the target device via CUDA managed memory or explicit device arrays.\n\n### 6.2 Multi-Node / MPI Placement\n\n`ChunkLayout.rank_assignment` maps each logical chunk to an MPI rank. For Phase 1, this is always all chunks to rank 0 (no MPI decomposition). Later phases extend to per-rank ownership with MPI halo exchange.\n\n**Separation of concerns:**\n- `ChunkSpec` is pure planning metadata — no field data, no communication\n- `ChunkLayout` adds device/rank placement hints\n- Actual field arrays and PML state are allocated at runtime using `ChunkSpec.local_grid_shape`\n- Halo exchange uses `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` to know which chunk pairs need to communicate\n\n### 6.3 Warp Kernel Conventions\n\nEach chunk's field arrays are Warp-compatible `wp.array` objects allocated on the target device. Warp kernel launches use chunk-local index ranges:\n\n```python\n# Pseudo-code for chunk-local kernel launch\nchunk = chunks[chunk_id]\nwp.launch(\n    electric_update_kernel,\n    dim=chunk.local_grid_shape,\n    inputs=[chunk.electric_field, chunk.magnetic_field, chunk.eps, chunk.mu],\n    device=chunk.device_id,\n)\n```\n\nHalo exchange is implemented as separate Warp kernels that read from neighbor chunks' field arrays and write to ghost cells.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Symmetry and Logical vs. Stored Topology\n\n### 7.1 Symmetry Reduction\n\nWhen `Simulation.symmetry` is non-zero, only the symmetry-reduced portion of the domain is stored. `ChunkSpec.is_reduced` and `ChunkSpec.symmetry_multiplicity` track which chunks are in the reduced region.\n\n`ChunkSpec.face_halos[\"x.minus\"].electric_signs` and `.magnetic_signs` carry the pre-computed reflection signs per face from the `SymmetryAxisIR` data. These are the same signs used for PEC/PMC boundaries — the symmetry transform is a logical address transform applied during the halo exchange.\n\n### 7.2 Periodic and Bloch Remapping\n\nFor periodic axes, the `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` connects the `plus` face of the last chunk to the `minus` face of the first chunk (and vice versa). For Bloch, the exchange includes the `phase_factor` from `BlochBoundaryIR`.\n\n**Complex field storage:** `BoundarySpecIR.requires_complex_fields=True` when any Bloch axis is present. This flag forces complex dtype for all field arrays even when `bloch_vec == 0` for that axis.\n\n---\n\n## 8. updated.\n\n    Array layout: E and H have shape (nx, ny, nz, 3) with\n    component order (Ex=0, Ey=1, Ez=2) for E and (Hx=0, Hy=1, Hz=2) for H.\n\n    Args:\n        H: Magnetic field array with shape (nx, ny, nz, 3).\n        E: Electric field array with shape (nx, ny, nz, 3).\n        mu_xx, mu_yy, mu_zz: Permeability arrays with shape (nx, ny, nz).\n        dt: Timestep size.\n        dx, dy, dz: Cell sizes.\n    \"\"\"\n    nx, ny, nz = H.shape[:3]\n    # Interior indices: [1, nx-2], [1, ny-2], [1, nz-2]\n    i1, i2 = 1, nx - 1\n    j1, j2 = 1, ny - 1\n    k1, k2 = 1, nz - 1\n\n    # Precompute 1/dy, 1/dz, 1/dx for efficiency\n    inv_dy = 1.0 / dy\n    inv_dz = 1.0 / dz\n    inv_dx = 1.0 / dx\n\n    # ---- Hx component update ----\n    # Hx: dEy/dz - dEz/dy\n    Ey = E[:, :, :, 1]  # shape (nx, ny, nz)\n    Ez = E[:, :, :, 2]\n\n    dEy_dz_Hx = (Ey[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1+1:k2+1] - Ey[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2]) * inv_dz\n    dEz_dy_Hx = (Ez[i1:i2, j1+1:j2+1, k1:k2] - Ez[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2]) * inv_dy\n\n    ch_Hx = -dt / (mu_xx[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2] + 1e-20)\n    H[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2, 0] += ch_Hx * (dEy_dz_Hx - dEz_dy_Hx)\n\n    # ---- Hy component update ----\n    # Hy: dEz/dx - dEx/dz\n    Ex = E[:, :, :, 0]\n\n    dEz_dx_Hy = (Ez[i1+1:i2+1, j1:j2, k1:k2] - Ez[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2]) * inv_dx\n    dEx_dz_Hy = (Ex[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1+1:k2+1] - Ex[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2]) * inv_dz\n\n    ch_Hy = -dt / (mu_yy[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2] + 1e-20)\n    H[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2, 1] += ch_Hy * (dEz_dx_Hy - dEx_dz_Hy)\n\n    # ---- Hz component update ----\n    # Hz: dEx/dy - dEy/dx\n    dEx_dy_Hz = (Ex[i1:i2, j1+1:j2+1, k1:k2] - Ex[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2]) * inv_dy\n    dEy_dx_Hz = (Ey[i1+1:i2+1, j1:j2, k1:k2] - Ey[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2]) * inv_dx\n\n    ch_Hz = -dt / (mu_zz[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2] + 1e-20)\n    H[i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2, 2] += ch_Hz * (dEx_dy_Hz - dEy_dx_Hz)\n\n\ndef allocate_maxwell_arrays(\n    grid_shape: tuple[int, int, int],\n    *,\n    complex_policy: ComplexFieldPolicy | None It provides:\n\n- Device management and GPU selection policies\n- Persistent array base types and allocation conventions\n- Module stability markers for JIT compilation\n- Capture-safe stepping protocol\n- Profiling hooks and instrumentation\n\nDesign Principles\n----------------\n1. **Module stability before JIT churn**: All kernels in a module compile together.\n   Stabilize module contents early to avoid reload churn.\n2. **Persistent arrays over temporaries**: Field buffers are allocated once and\n   reused across timesteps to minimize allocation overhead.\n3. **Capture-safe stepping**: Kernels must not capture mutable state from the\n   outer Python scope. All timestep-dependent values must be passed as arguments.\n4. **Explicit device placement**: Arrays carry device affinity explicitly rather\n   than relying on global state.\n5. **Structured profiling**: Use Warp's ScopedTimer and NVTX markers for\n   GPU-side instrumentation, with CPU-side timing hooks for end-to-end metrics.\n\nDevice Management\n-----------------\n- Use ``get_warp_device()`` to obtain the default device or a specific GPU.\n- For multi-GPU: map logical chunk indices to device IDs via\n  ``ChunkLayout.device_assignment``.\n- All array allocations use the target device explicitly.\n\nArray Conventions\n----------------\n- Field arrays: ``wp.array(dtype=wp.float32 or wp.complex64, shape=(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3))``\n- Coefficient arrays: ``wp.array(dtype=wp.float32, shape=(Nx, Ny, Nz))``\n- Auxiliary state: ``wp.array(dtype=wp.complex64, shape=(num_poles, Nx, Ny, Nz))``\n- All arrays are allocated on the target device; no managed memory unless explicit.\n\nDtype Policy\n-----------\n- Single precision (float32/complex64) is the default for GPU execution.\n- Double precision (float64/complex128) is available but may significantly\n  reduce performance on consumer NVIDIA GPUs.\n- Complex fields are required when any Bloch boundary is present.\n- The ``requires_complex_fields`` flag from ``BoundarySpecIR`` determines whether\n  to use complex dtype for field storage.\n\nModule Stability\n---------------\nUse ``mark_module_stable()`` after defining all kernels in a module.\nThis signals that the module's kernel set is frozen and ready for JIT.\nDuring development, unstable modules trigger a warning on import.\n\nCapture-Safe Stepping\n---------------------\nEvery kernel function that depends on timestep-varying values (dt, time, step_index)\nmust receive those values as explicit arguments. Do NOT capture them from closure.\n\nExample::\n\n    # BAD - captures dt from outer scope\n    @wp.kernel\n    def bad_update(E, H,):\n        dt = outer_dt  # captured!\n        ...\n\n    # GOOD - dt passed explicitly\n    @wp.kernel\n    def good_update(E, H, dt: float):\n        ...\n\nCapture-safe stepping also means:\n- Source amplitudes are computed outside the kernel and passed as arrays or scalars\n- Monitor intervals are evaluated in Python before calling recording kernels\n- Boundary coefficients are pre-compiled and passed as array arguments\n\nProfiling Hooks\n---------------\n- ``WarpTimer`` context manager for GPU-side kernel timing\n- ``nvtx_range`` for annotating execution phases\n- ``step_metrics()`` helper for computing cells/s and Gcells/s\n\nReferences\n----------\n- Warp docs: https://docs.nvidia.com/warp-py\n- GPU Benchmarking: ``../papers/gpu_benchmarking.pdf``\n- Chunk Contract: ``../phase1/architecture/chunk-contract.md``\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Any, Literal\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"WARP_AVAILABLE\",\n    \"wp\",\n    \"get_warp_device\",\n    \"get_default_device\",","numLines":100,"startLine":1,"totalLines":692}}}
